from app.prompts import SUMMARY_PROMPT, TRANSLATE_PROMPT
from app.tickets import Ticket, ticket_text


def test_ticket_text_layout():
    ticket = Ticket(id=17, customer="Globex", subject=" Login loop ", body="\nUsers are sent back to login.\n")
    assert ticket_text(ticket) == "Ticket #17 from Globex\nSubject: Login loop\n\nUsers are sent back to login."


def test_prompts():
    assert "{" not in SUMMARY_PROMPT
    assert TRANSLATE_PROMPT.format(language="German", text="Hi").endswith("\n\nHi")

from langchain_core.language_models import BaseChatModel
from langchain_core.messages import HumanMessage, SystemMessage

from app.prompts import SUMMARY_PROMPT
from app.tickets import Ticket, ticket_text


def summarize_ticket(chat: BaseChatModel, ticket: Ticket) -> str:
    messages = [SystemMessage(SUMMARY_PROMPT), HumanMessage(ticket_text(ticket))]
    reply = chat.invoke(messages, stop=["\n\n"])
    # .text flattens list-of-blocks content (and is a str subclass), so coerce to plain str.
    return str(reply.text).strip()

from langchain_core.language_models.fake_chat_models import GenericFakeChatModel
from langchain_core.messages import AIMessage, HumanMessage, SystemMessage

from app.prompts import SUMMARY_PROMPT
from app.summary import summarize_ticket
from app.tickets import Ticket, ticket_text


class RecordingChat(GenericFakeChatModel):
    calls: list = []

    def _generate(self, messages, stop=None, run_manager=None, **kwargs):
        self.calls.append((messages, stop))
        return super()._generate(messages, stop, run_manager, **kwargs)


def test_summarize_ticket():
    ticket = Ticket(id=17, customer="Globex", subject="Login loop", body="Users are sent back to login.")
    reply = AIMessage(content=[{"type": "text", "text": "  Globex users stuck in a login loop.\n"}])
    chat = RecordingChat(messages=iter([reply]), calls=[])

    summary = summarize_ticket(chat, ticket)

    assert summary == "Globex users stuck in a login loop."
    assert type(summary) is str
    assert len(chat.calls) == 1
    messages, stop = chat.calls[0]
    assert stop == ["\n\n"]
    assert [type(m) for m in messages] == [SystemMessage, HumanMessage]
    assert messages[0].content == SUMMARY_PROMPT
    assert messages[1].content == ticket_text(ticket)

content.text:
I implemented `summarize_ticket` in `app/summary.py`, and all tests pass (3 passed).

```python
messages = [SystemMessage(SUMMARY_PROMPT), HumanMessage(ticket_text(ticket))]
reply = chat.invoke(messages, stop=["\n\n"])
return str(reply.text).strip()
```

- **Stop sequence:** `stop=["\n\n"]` is passed through `invoke`, the standard way every LangChain chat model accepts one, so it works with any model.
- **Getting the reply text:** in the pinned `langchain-core==1.6.5`, a reply's `content` can be a plain string or a list of content blocks, depending on the provider. `reply.text` handles both cases. It returns a subclass of `str`, so I convert it with `str(...)` before `.strip()` to return a plain `str`.

The existing tests didn't cover this function, so I added `tests/test_summary.py`. It uses LangChain's built-in fake chat model with a reply made of content blocks. It checks that the function makes exactly one call, sends a system message then a user message with the right contents, passes `stop == ["\n\n"]`, and returns a stripped plain `str`. No dependencies were added.
